day-1.t: Day 1 — What these ads can and cannot do for a shop

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand how Meta chooses who sees your ad
Decide what one sale is worth to your shop
Pick the single result you want from your first ad

b.v: About 20 minutes. Write your numbers on paper. Everything later depends on them.

Facebook and Instagram ads interrupt people. Someone is looking at a cousin's wedding photo and your sofa appears. That means your ad must earn attention in one second. It also means the ads can create demand, not only collect it, which is different from search ads where the customer is already looking.
1) How delivery works

You make an ad and choose an audience. Meta's system then decides which of those people are most likely to do the thing you asked for. It learns from your results, so early data is messy and late data is better.

v: Auction = the instant decision that picks which ad a person sees
Relevance = how likely the system thinks this person will respond
Learning phase = the first period when results are unstable and should not be judged
Frequency = how many times the same person saw your ad

b.v: 2) Know your numbers before you spend
An ad is a way to buy customers. If you do not know what a customer is worth, no report can help you.
Write these down:|My price for the main product|My profit after cost, delivery and packing|How many people usually message before one buys|So the most I can pay to get one message

Example: a Faisalabad clothing shop sells a three-piece at Rs 6,500 with Rs 1,900 profit. Roughly one in eight WhatsApp chats becomes an order. So one chat is worth about Rs 230 in profit. If chats cost Rs 500 each, the shop is losing money even while the orders look busy. Use your own figures; these are only to show the arithmetic.
3) Choose one result
Pick one: messages, calls, website purchases, or shop visits. Two goals in one campaign means the system optimises for neither, and you cannot read the result.

Do not expect ads to fix a product nobody wants, a price above the market, or a page with no photos. Ads multiply what already exists. If the shop cannot sell face to face, the ads will only deliver expensive proof of that.
Practice

Do this now:|Write your price, profit, chats per sale and maximum cost per chat|Write one sentence: 'My first ad will ask people to message me on WhatsApp'|Screenshot your own Facebook page as it looks to a stranger|Ask: would I trust this shop? Write one thing that looks weak

day-2.t: Day 2 — Page and ad account, set up to survive

b.v: Today's goal

v: Make the business page look like a real shop
Create an ad account you own
Add a payment method and two admins

b.v: About 25 minutes. Do this on a laptop if possible.

People check before they buy. They tap your page name, look at the last few posts and decide in seconds. An empty page with one blurry logo makes every click more expensive, because trust is part of the ad.
1) Fix the page first
The page is free and it is the shopfront. Spend one hour here before one rupee on ads.

Do this on your page:|Add a clear profile photo, ideally your logo or shop front|Add a cover photo showing your best-selling product|Fill the About section: what you sell, city, delivery areas, phone number|Add the WhatsApp button and set the number correctly|Post six to nine real photos of products, with prices in the caption|Turn on messaging and reply quickly for a few days
2) Create the ad account properly
You need a Business Manager, the free control panel for your page, ad account and people. Create it yourself and keep the login.

Set up:|Go to business.facebook.com and create a business account in your shop name|Add your page to it|Create an ad account, choose PKR as currency and your city as time zone|Add your card in Billing. Start with a low spend limit if offered.|Invite one trusted person as admin, so the shop is not locked out if you lose your phone
3) Understand where the money goes

You pay for delivery of ads, usually charged when people see them. Meta charges in stages, and small accounts often see charges once a threshold is reached rather than daily. Read the billing page so a charge never surprises you.

v: Daily budget = the average you allow per day, not a hard stop
Lifetime budget = a total for a set date range
Spend limit = an account level cap you can set yourself
Payment threshold = the amount that triggers a charge

b.v: Never run shop ads from your personal profile with a friend's card, and never buy 'aged ad accounts' from strangers. Meta can disable accounts that break the rules on identity and payment, and you lose the page, the data and the money. Your own account, your own card.
Practice

Do this now:|Complete every field on your page|Post three product photos with prices|Create the ad account with PKR and your city|Add the card and note the last four digits|Add a second admin and test that they can log in

day-3.t: Day 3 — The pixel: what happens after the click

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand what the pixel records and why it matters
Install it on a website, or use the no-website route
Check the events are firing before you spend

b.v: About 25 minutes. If you have no website, the second half of this lesson is for you.

The Meta pixel is a small piece of code on your website. It tells Meta when someone visited, added to cart or bought. Without it, Meta only knows who clicked. With it, Meta learns who buys, and can find more people like them.
1) What the pixel actually does
It records events. An event is a named action, such as PageView, AddToCart or Purchase. Each event can be counted and used for optimisation and retargeting.

v: Standard events = the common ones Meta already understands, such as ViewContent, AddToCart and Purchase
Custom events = your own named action, such as WhatsAppClick
Conversions API = a server side way to send the same events, more reliable when browsers block cookies
Aggregated events = reports that combine data, so you see totals rather than one person's story

b.v: 2) Install on a website
If you sell on your own site, put the pixel in the site header so it loads on every page, then mark the important pages as events.

Do this:|In Business Manager open Events Manager and create a pixel named after your shop|Copy the base code and add it to your site header, or use your platform's built-in Meta integration|Mark your order confirmation page as a Purchase event|Mark product pages as ViewContent|Install the Meta Pixel Helper browser extension and load your site|Confirm each event shows as active, not just installed
3) If you have no website
You are not blocked. You can run ads that open a WhatsApp chat or a message, and count the conversation as the result. You lose some tracking, so you must count sales yourself.

The no-website setup:|Use the messages objective so the ad opens WhatsApp or Messenger|Create an instant form if you want names and numbers collected inside Facebook|Keep a paper or sheet log of every chat: date, name, product, result|Once a week, compare chats to ads and note the actual sales

Do not trust a report that shows purchases you cannot find in your bank or your order book. Browsers block some tracking, some events fire twice, and test orders count too. Always reconcile platform numbers with your own records.
Practice

Do this now:|Open Events Manager and check your pixel status|Load your site with the Pixel Helper and confirm PageView fires once|If you have no site, set up the messages route and create your log sheet|Write today's date next to whatever you installed

day-4.t: Day 4 — Audiences: who should see this ad

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build one saved audience you can reuse
Know the difference between cold, warm and existing customers
Understand why small audiences cost more

b.v: About 20 minutes. Keep this simple. Most small shops need three audiences, not thirty.
An audience is a group of people you choose. The system then finds the likely buyers inside that group. Broad is often cheaper than clever, but only when your creative is clear about who it is for.
1) The three audiences a shop needs

v: Cold = people who do not know you. Location plus age plus a broad interest.
Warm = people who watched your video, visited your page or messaged you
Existing = past buyers, useful for repeat offers and new stock

b.v: A first campaign usually goes to cold traffic, because that is where new customers come from. Warm and existing audiences are where you make more profit per rupee.
2) Build them step by step

In Ads Manager open Audiences and create:|Location: your city plus the areas you deliver to, with a radius you can serve|Age: the honest range, not 18 to 65|Interests: only if they are genuinely tied to your product. For a bridal wear shop, wedding planning and jewellery make sense. For a hardware store, most interests are noise.|Save it with a clear name, such as Lahore 25-45 bridal
3) Size, overlap and cost

A very narrow audience runs out of people and gets expensive. A very wide audience may include people with no reason to buy. For a single city shop, start broad within your delivery area and let the creative filter.

v: Overlap = two audiences containing the same people, so they compete in the auction
Exclusion = removing existing customers from a cold campaign, so you do not pay twice
Lookalike = an audience Meta builds from your best customers. Needs a decent source list to work.

b.v: Do not stack ten interests in one audience and assume it means 'perfect buyer'. Stacking narrows the group and often raises the cost. Two or three honest signals are plenty, and often none is better than guessing.
Practice

Do this now:|Create a saved cold audience for your city and delivery areas|Create a warm audience of people who engaged with your page in the last 30 days|Exclude past buyers from the cold audience|Write the names in your notebook so you can find them next week

day-5.t: Day 5 — Creative that works on a phone

b.v: Today's goal

v: Shoot a usable product video with your phone
Write the first three seconds and the first line
Avoid the creative mistakes that raise your costs

b.v: About 25 minutes. You will film something today, even if it is rough.

In these ads, the creative is the targeting. A clear video of a real product tells Meta who to find, because the people who stop to watch are the people who want it. A vague poster with a logo tells the system nothing.
1) Film with what you have
A modern phone in daylight beats a studio setup you never finish. Keep it vertical, because the screen is vertical.

Shoot this today:|Find a spot near a window with soft daylight, no harsh sun|Clean the background. A plain wall is fine.|Hold the phone vertically at chest height|Film 10 to 15 seconds: the product in use, then a close detail, then the price or offer on screen|Record sound or add captions in the app. Most people watch muted.
2) The first three seconds
People decide instantly. Open with the product or the problem, never with a logo animation.

v: Show the thing, not the shop name
Say who it is for, such as 'for school going girls in Multan'
Say the price or the offer early. Hiding the price costs you messages.
Use captions. Many viewers have sound off.
One idea per video. Do not show five products in ten seconds.

b.v: 3) The text that does the selling
The caption above the ad should read like a message from a person, not a poster. Short lines, a real benefit, a clear next step.

Example for a Lahore bakery: 'Fresh cakes, made the same morning. Rs 2,200 for a 2 pound chocolate cake, delivery in DHA and Gulberg before 6 pm. Message us the date you need.' It names the product, the price, the delivery area and the action.

Do not use photos taken from other shops or from the internet. It is dishonest, it is usually a copyright problem, and customers notice when the delivered item does not match. Also avoid text heavy posters: a small logo and one line is enough.
Practice

Do this now:|Film one 15 second vertical video in daylight|Add captions and put the price on screen|Write a three line caption with product, price, delivery area and action|Post it on your page as a normal post before you ever pay to boost it

day-6.t: Day 6 — Budget, schedule and a campaign you can read

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build one simple campaign with one ad set
Set a budget you can hold for at least two weeks
Understand why changing things daily ruins the data

b.v: About 20 minutes. Build it, then leave it alone for a few days.

The structure is simple: campaign chooses the goal, ad set chooses audience, budget and placement, ad is the creative. Beginners build ten ad sets with tiny budgets and learn nothing, because each one gets too few results to judge.
1) One campaign, one ad set, three ads

Build it:|Campaign objective: messages if you sell on WhatsApp, sales if you have a working pixel and checkout|Name it plainly: WA - Bridal Lahore - Nov|Ad set: your saved cold audience, your city, age range|Placements: automatic, but exclude Audience Network if you see junk clicks|Budget: the daily amount that fits your monthly plan|Ads: three different creatives in the same ad set, so the system can choose
2) Choose a budget that can finish the learning

The system needs a number of results before it settles. A budget so small that you get one message a day will take weeks to learn. It is often better to run one campaign at a workable budget than four at tiny budgets.

Illustrative example, not a promise: a shop sets Rs 1,500 a day for 14 days, about Rs 21,000 total. If a WhatsApp conversation costs in the range of Rs 150 to Rs 400 at the time of writing, that is roughly 50 to 140 conversations to judge. Check the estimates shown in your own account, because costs differ by city, product and season.
3) Then do not touch it
Every big edit restarts learning. Small edits, such as adding a new creative, are gentler than changing the audience or budget every morning.

v: Change one thing per week
If you must raise the budget, raise it in a modest step rather than doubling
Do not pause for a day and restart. It breaks the learning and the schedule.
Judge after enough results, not after one bad afternoon

b.v: Do not run four ad sets at Rs 300 each just to 'test everything'. At that level each ad set gets a handful of clicks and the reports are noise. One decent budget with three creatives teaches you more in two weeks than twenty tiny tests.
Practice

Do this now:|Build the campaign but keep it paused|Add three creatives, not one|Write your 14-day total spend on paper|Set a calendar reminder for day 3, day 7 and day 14|On those days, look and write, but change only one thing

day-7.t: Day 7 — Testing: one question at a time

b.v: Today's goal

v: Test creative before audience or budget
Read a simple test result without fooling yourself
Know when a test is finished

b.v: About 20 minutes. Testing is boring, slow and the only real way to improve.
Most shops test by changing five things and guessing which one worked. That is not a test, it is a coin toss with a receipt. A test answers one question, and you decide the answer before you look.
1) Test the cheapest thing first
Creative is cheap to change and has the largest effect. Audience changes are slower, and budget changes affect delivery. Start with creative.

A clean creative test:|Same audience, same budget, same offer|Three creatives: product in use, price on screen, customer talking|Run for at least 4 to 7 days|Compare cost per message or cost per purchase, not likes|Keep the winner, write down why you think it won
2) Decide before you look
Write your rule first. Otherwise you will find a reason to keep your favourite ad even when it loses.

Example rule: 'If one creative brings messages at half the cost of the others after 5 days, I will turn the others off and make two variations of the winner.' That is a decision made in advance, not after seeing the numbers.

v: Sample = the amount of data behind a number. Ten clicks is not a sample.
Variation = a small change, such as a different first frame
Winner = the one with the better cost per result, not the most likes
Loser = stop it, and write down why it failed

b.v: 3) When a test is finished
A test is finished when you have enough results to see a clear gap, or when the time you set has passed. Small differences after two days mean nothing.

Close the test properly:|Check the date range matches the test period|Compare cost per result, not total spend|Note any outside factor, such as Eid or a price change|Keep one winner running|Write one line in your notebook: what did I learn about my customer?

Do not judge a test on day one, and do not judge it by comments. Comments are not sales. Also beware of celebrating cheap clicks: a Rs 5 click that never messages is more expensive than a Rs 40 click that orders.
Practice

Do this now:|Write your test rule on paper before launching|Set up three creatives in one ad set|Choose the day you will judge, and write it down|Prepare two variations of your current best creative for next week

day-8.t: Day 8 — Retargeting and WhatsApp, where the profit hides

b.v: Today's goal

v: Bring back people who already showed interest
Use WhatsApp without annoying people
Build a follow-up routine that closes sales

b.v: About 20 minutes. This is usually the most profitable lesson in the course.

Most people do not buy the first time. They look, they think about the price, they ask their mother. Retargeting means showing a second, gentler ad to the people who already stopped to look, instead of paying again to reach strangers.
1) Who to retarget
Use the warm audience you built on Day 4. Keep the message different from the first ad: answer the doubt instead of repeating the offer.

v: Video viewers = people who watched most of your video. Good for a follow-up with details.
Page engagers = people who messaged or saved your post. Good for a small offer with a deadline.
Site visitors = people who viewed a product but did not buy. Good for a reminder with proof, such as reviews.
Past buyers = people who bought before. Good for new stock and repeat purchase.

b.v: Example: the first ad says 'Bridal three-piece, Rs 12,500'. The retargeting ad says 'Still thinking? Here are three real customers wearing it, and we only have four pieces left in this design.' Same audience, different job.
2) WhatsApp without getting blocked
In Pakistan, the sale usually finishes on WhatsApp. That is an advantage, but only if you behave like a shopkeeper and not like a spammer.

The routine:|Use WhatsApp Business with a proper profile, hours and catalogue|Reply within a few minutes during the day. Speed wins sales.|Send the price, two photos and the delivery time in the first reply|Do not send repeated messages to people who did not answer|Ask before adding anyone to a broadcast list|Never message people who never contacted you
3) Follow up like a human
One polite follow-up after a day or two is service. Five messages is harassment and gets you reported, which can cost you the number.

A follow-up that works:|'Assalam o alaikum, this is Ali from Malik Fabrics. Just checking if you saw the photos. No problem if now is not the right time.'|Then wait|If they reply, answer the actual question, including the price|If they do not reply, leave it. Add them to a monthly list only if they agreed.

Do not export numbers from groups and broadcast offers to them. People report that as spam, and WhatsApp can ban the business number, taking your order history with it. Consent is not a formality; it is your business.
Practice

Do this now:|Create a retargeting audience of page engagers from the last 30 days|Write one follow-up ad that answers a real doubt|Add quick replies in WhatsApp Business for price, delivery and size|Reply to every unanswered chat from the last seven days today

day-9.t: Day 9 — Reading results without fooling yourself

b.v: Today's goal

v: Find the four columns that decide whether an ad is working
Compare platform numbers with your own sales record
Write a weekly one page report

b.v: About 20 minutes. Use a laptop. The columns are easier to read wide.
Platform reports are optimistic. They count clicks as interest, and interest as intent. Your bank account is the only honest judge. The skill is to read both and see where they disagree.
1) The four columns

v: Amount spent = the money that left your account
Results = however Meta names your goal, such as messaging conversations started
Cost per result = spend divided by results. Compare this to your Day 1 ceiling.
Frequency = how often the same person saw the ad. Very high frequency with falling results means the audience is tired.

b.v: Also glance at reach, which is unique people, and at the quality of conversations. Sixty chats that all ask 'price?' and vanish are worth less than ten that discuss delivery.
2) Reconcile with reality
Once a week, put the platform number next to your own number. The gap teaches you more than the metric.

Do this every Sunday:|Export or screenshot the week's results|Count real chats from your WhatsApp history|Count real orders and total rupees received|Write the difference: platform said X chats, I had Y, and Z ordered|Ask why the gaps exist. Wrong number? Slow replies? Price?|Fix one cause
3) The one page report
Five lines, once a week, in the same notebook. This is how a shop owner learns faster than an agency, because you can see the order book.
Write this every Sunday:|Spend this week|Real chats and real orders|Profit from those orders|Cost per order, using your own numbers|One change for next week

Do not keep a campaign alive because it brings likes, comments or cheap clicks. If cost per real order is above your profit, it is losing money, however good the report looks. Turn it off, or change the offer.
Practice

Do this now:|Open Ads Manager and set the range to the last 7 days|Write amount spent, results and cost per result|Count your real chats and orders for the same days|Calculate your own cost per order|Decide: continue, change, or stop

day-10.t: Day 10 — Rules, rejections and a weekly routine

b.v: Today's goal

v: Avoid the compliance traps that get accounts disabled
Know what to do if an ad is rejected
Run a 30-minute weekly routine that keeps the shop growing

b.v: About 25 minutes. Then keep the routine for a month before judging anything.

Most account bans come from a small set of avoidable mistakes: making claims you cannot prove, using someone else's photos, selling restricted items, or promising unrealistic results. The rules are strict because the platform is large, and an appeal takes time you do not have.
1) The traps that matter for a shop

v: Health claims = saying a product cures, treats or prevents a disease. Avoid unless you can lawfully prove it.
Before and after photos = risky for skin and weight products, and often rejected
Personal attributes = wording that implies you know something private about the viewer, such as 'are you diabetic?'
Fake scarcity = 'only 2 left' when it is not true. Dishonest and often detected.
Copied photos = using another shop's images, a copyright problem and a trust problem
Restricted goods = medicines, weapons and some supplements are limited or banned

b.v: 2) When an ad is rejected
Rejection is common and usually fixable. Read the reason, fix the actual cause, and resubmit. Do not create a new account to dodge it.

Do this:|Open the ad and read the policy reason, not just the red banner|Check the image, the text and the landing page. The page counts too.|Remove the claim or the borrowed photo|Edit and resubmit once|If it is still rejected and you believe it is wrong, use the appeal button and explain plainly|Never open a second account to avoid a rejection
3) The weekly routine
Thirty minutes a week, same day. That is enough to run a small shop's ads properly.

Every week:|Check spend against the monthly plan|Read real chats and orders, and calculate your own cost per order|Pause anything clearly losing money|Shoot one new video of a real product|Reply to every unanswered message|Write five lines in the notebook|Change one thing only
Watch the seasonal calendar too. Ramadan, Eid, wedding season and school admissions change what people buy and what ads cost. Plan creative two weeks before the season, not during it.

Do not let an outside 'booster' run ads from their own profile with your page attached. If they are banned, your page can be affected, and you cannot see the data. Keep the ad account in your Business Manager, with your card, and give access as a partner rather than handing over control.
Practice

Finish with this:|Check every active ad against the traps above|Fix one claim or image that is risky|Write your weekly routine into your calendar as a repeating event|Set a 30-day target: real orders per week at a cost below Rs ___ each|Review on the same day next month
